explanations: The actor is taken from `changedBy` in the request body, falling back to the authenticated user only if the client omits it. Any payroll_admin can send `changedBy: "<someone else>"` and the audit trail will attribute a salary or bank-account change to another person, defeating non-repudiation. The actor must come only from the authenticated identity (`req.user.id`); a client-supplied value may at most be stored as a separate, untrusted field.

For field === 'bankAccount', write() replaces each value with `maskAccount(v)#fingerprint(v)`: asterisks plus the last four digits, followed by 16 hex chars of a SHA-256 hash. Plain text is never stored for this field, both old and new are kept, and the value is not reduced to just the last four digits.

repo.updateField runs and completes before audit.write; there is no transaction spanning both. When insert throws, the rejection escapes the async handler before res.status(204), so no 204 is sent, but the employee record is already updated with no audit entry. Nothing reverts it or retries the audit.
router.use installs a middleware that responds 403 unless req.user has the payroll_admin role. It runs before the PATCH handler, so validation, the update, and the audit write never happen.
